nodes.name: TiO2 seeds formation
nodes.procedure: The CFP (3×3 cm²) was pretreated in a plasma cleaning instrument. The CFP was immersed in a C16H36O4Ti ethanol solution (obtained by dissolving 0.32 g C16H36O4Ti in 20.0 mL anhydrous ethanol), ultrasonicated for 40 min, then annealed in a muffle furnace at 400°C for 30 min. This formed the TiO2 seeds on the surface of the CFP.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, TiO2 nanowires were grown on the CFP using a hydrothermal method. The CFP was immersed in a C16H36O4Ti ethanol solution... annealed in a muffle furnace at 400°C for 30 min.

nodes.name: TiO2 nanowires growth
nodes.procedure: Next, 15 mL HCl, 15 mL acetone, and 1.5 mL C16H36O4Ti were added into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave (50 mL volume) and the CFP coated with TiO2 seeds was dipped into the solution. The hydrothermal reaction was maintained at a constant temperature of 200°C for 80 min in an electric oven and then cooled at room temperature. The sample was then sonicated with deionized water for 10 min and dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 6 h.
nodes.source_text: Next, 15 mL HCl, 15 mL acetone, and 1.5 mL C16H36O4Ti were added into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave... dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: TiN formation by ammoniation
nodes.procedure: Finally, the samples were annealed in NH3 at 900°C for 3 h with a heating rate of 3°C min^-1 to produce the CFP supported TiN.
nodes.source_text: Finally, the samples were annealed in NH3 at 900°C for 3 h with a heating rate of 3°C min^-1 to produce the CFP supported TiN.

nodes.name: Ru NPs impregnation-reduction
nodes.procedure: The CFP supported TiN was immersed in 5 mL 20 mg mL^-1 RuCl3·H2O aqueous solution and stirred for 24 h, then annealed in a tube furnace at 500°C for 2 h at a heating rate of 3°C min^-1 under an Ar/H2 atmosphere to obtain CFP supported Ru NPs/TiN.
nodes.source_text: The CFP supported TiN was immersed in 5 mL 20 mg mL^-1 RuCl3·H2O aqueous solution and stirred for 24 h, then annealed in a tube furnace at 500°C for 2 h...

nodes.name: NiFe LDH hydrothermal growth
nodes.procedure: 0.15 g of Ni(NO3)2, 0.20 g of Fe(NO3)3, and 0.38 g of urea were dissolved in 36 mL of deionized water. Once dissolved, the solution was transferred into a 50 ml autoclave containing a piece of Ni foam positioned against the wall. The hydrothermal synthesis was conducted at 120°C in an electric oven for 6 hours.
nodes.source_text: The NiFe LDH/Ni foam electrodes were prepared via a hydrothermal growth method... conducted at 120°C in an electric oven for 6 hours.

nodes.name: NiMoFeOx hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Firstly, the commercial NF was washed with 1 M HCl and distilled water. Next, one piece of NF (3 cm²×3 cm²) was immersed in 30 mL H2O containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.04 M), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.02 M) and Na2MoO4·2H2O (0.01 M) in a 50 ml autoclave, then reacted at 150°C in an electric oven for 6 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows uniform Ru NP distribution on TiN; lattice spacings 0.211 nm (TiN(200)) and 0.208 nm (Ru(101)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g shows the typical low-magnification high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image of Ru NPs/TiN, which indicates the uniform adherence of the Ru nanoparticles to the substrate ... measured lattice spacing of 0.211 nm is attributed to the (200) plane of cubic TiN. The hexagonal close-packed (hcp) lattice with a lattice spacing of 0.208 nm is assigned to the (101) plane of the Ru nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mappings reveal homogeneous distribution of Ti, N and Ru elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning TEM coupled with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDX) mappings reveals a homogeneous distribution of Ti, N and Ru (Fig. 1c–f).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows coexistence of metallic Ru and oxidized Ru; Ti 2p peaks positively shifted compared to pure TiN indicating electron transfer from TiN to Ru NPs; N 1s shows positively shifted Ti-N bond and Ru-Nx bond peak confirming strong Ru-TiN interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of Ru NPs/TiN suggests the coexistence of metallic Ru and oxidized Ru (Fig. 2a). In the high-resolution Ti 2p XPS spectrum (Figure S7a), Ru NPs/TiN were positively shifted compared to pure TiN, indicating electron transfer from the TiN substrate to the Ru nanoparticles ... Moreover, the RuNx bond peak can be clearly observed in the N 1s spectrum of Ru NPs/TiN, suggesting strong anchoring of the Ru nanoparticles to the substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES absorption intensity between RuO2 and Ru foil; edge energy shifted higher than Ru foil but less than RuO2/Ru/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2b, the K-edge absorption intensity of Ru in Ru NPs/TiN fell between that of RuO2 and Ru foil, and it was also lower than that of Ru/C. Moreover, compared to the Ru foil, the edge energy of Ru NPs/TiN (Fig. 2c) was shifted to higher energy, but less than that of RuO2 and Ru/C.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows predominant peak at 1.6 Å for Ru-N/O scattering path and peak at 2.4 Å for Ru-Ru coordination; fitting gives coordination numbers of ~5.7 for Ru-N/O and 2.4 for Ru-Ru bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transforms of the phase-uncorrected EXAFS (Fig. 2d, and Supplementary Fig. S8) show a predominant peak around 1.6 Å for Ru NPs/TiN, matching the Ru−N/O scattering path ... The EXAFS fitting curves of Ru NPs/TiN at the Ru k space (Fig. 2d and Supplementary Fig. S9) and the corresponding fitting parameters (Supplementary Table S2) suggest that the coordination numbers of Ru−N/O and Ru−Ru bonds are ~5.7 and 2.4, respectively.
